title: Nearly 197 million Indian workers in jobs vulnerable to AI automation, finds Great Lakes Institute study
key_facts: A paper titled 'AI, Automation and India's Workforce: Who Gains, Who's Exposed, and How Policy Can Shape the Future' was released on Sunday 11 Oct 2026 by the Centre for Finance and Economics Research at the Great Lakes Institute of Management, Chennai.
Authors: Vidya Mahambare, Vivek Jadhav and Vishnu Venugopalan.
Nearly 197 million Indian workers are in jobs with a high share of routine tasks that could eventually be automated; about 46 million work in occupations where AI could improve productivity.
About 150.5 million workers, 24.6% of the working-age population, are in AI-exposed occupations.
39.4% of employed people aged 15-24 work in routine-heavy jobs, rising to 55% in urban areas.
Kerala has the highest AI exposure (42%), then Haryana (37.9%) and Tamil Nadu (32.9%); Punjab has the highest share of routine-task jobs (44.6%).
Of AI-exposed women's work, 37.6% is AI-complementary, against 28.4% for men; only about 18% of women aged 20-29 are in paid work, against about 79% of men.
The authors urge early AI education in schools, wider access to AI tools and training for young people and routine-task workers.
quote_evidence: The report estimates that around 197 million workers are in jobs where routine tasks could eventually be automated.
This does not mean all these jobs will disappear, but it highlights the scale of the workforce that could be affected by automation.
Prudence, however, calls for acting early rather than waiting
why_it_matters_hint: An estimate of how many Indian workers are exposed to AI task automation, with young urban workers most exposed.
notes: Full text read. Figures are the study's own estimates of exposure, not forecasts of job losses; not checked independently.
